newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SOCCER-INDONESIA THROUGH TO TIGER CUP SEMIFINALS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-INDONESIA THROUGH TO TIGER CUP SEMIFINALS.

text.p: Indonesia, scoring five goals in the first 40 minutes, became the first team to qualify for the semifinals of the Tiger Cup when they beat Burma 6-1 on Monday.

Man-of-the-match Peri Sandria and captain Fachri Husaini each scored twice to give Indonesia, second-favourites for the title, maximum points from their first three games and guaranteed them a semifinal berth with one group A match still to come for them.
Husaini opened the scoring in the seventh minute and closed it in the 65th, each time bursting through the middle of the Burmese defence before striking the ball low into the net.
Sandria opened his account in the 21st minute with a left-foot strike which slid under the goalkeeper to make it 2-0.
Maung Maung Htay appeared to bring Burma back into the game with a 26th-minute goal but less than 60 seconds later Sandria restored the lead when he blasted the ball into the roof of the net.
Indonesia's advantage was increased by Ansyari Lubis in the 28th minute and, in the 39th minute, Eri Iriyanto's penalty put the result beyond doubt.
In the evening's other game, Cambodia finished the competition without a point as they lost 1-0 to Laos, their fourth defeat in the tournament.
Homsonbath Khonsavanh's 39th-minute goal gave Laos their first win to add to a surprise 1-1 draw with Vietnam in their opening match.
